Failing source and output are retained under docs/gams-candidates/amosf90. The checked driver uses upper-right-quadrant arguments and excludes this case; no source patch or tolerance relaxation is applied.

Typed LAPACK interfaces. The checked real64 main verifies a matrix inverse residual, determinant, known eigenvalues, eigenpair residuals and orthonormality for a symmetric 3-by-3 tridiagonal matrix. Complex, single-precision and other BLAS/LAPACK wrappers are not covered. Legacy implicit external interfaces are explicitly enabled in the pinned package manifest.

Complex, single-precision and other BLAS/LAPACK wrappers are not covered. Legacy implicit external interfaces are explicitly enabled in the pinned package manifest. Dedicated D4 driver checks all 20 eigenpairs of the same Dirichlet tridiagonal matrix used by the ARPACK driver against analytic eigenvalues and sign-invariant sine eigenvectors, with residuals, orthonormality and reconstruction. This covers a real symmetric ordinary problem only; no generic solver success status is inferred from the API return. Refined from broad D4 to D4a1 for the reviewed real symmetric ordinary-eigenproblem interfaces.

Growable integer vectors. The checked main verifies growth from a two-element capacity, appended arrays, stable duplicate removal, remove/delete/pop and final compaction against independent expected contents. A checksum-guarded one-line edit fixes aliasing in unique: remove the already saved first value instead of the first array element while that array is being compacted. Empty-vector unique and all invalid-input cases are not covered.

Character-by-character text scanning. The main reconstructs a configuration record through current/next, verifies navigation and end boundaries, and checks that peek does not move the cursor. The recovered fields are converted with ordinary internal READ and compared with known values; this is a small parser example, not a full parsing language.

JSON parsing and serialization with explicit error values. The main checks numeric/string fields, missing-key reporting, compact serialization round trips and malformed-input rejection. It uses the original Erloff 2.2.0 API with a pinned compatible Strff 3.1.1 and ISO varying string 3.0.3; the Strff 4.0 dependency graph needs an unavailable GitHub mirror. No computational source is patched.

Typed process command-line parsing. The main launches itself once with fixed example arguments, then checks an integer, double, string, logical flag and untouched default. No supplied files or playground argument-setting changes are needed. Error exits, positional/named arguments, truncation and every syntax variant are not covered.

Key/value configuration input. The main creates and reads a tiny INI-style file with a section, comment, integer, double, logical and string, verifies known values and deletes it. A checksum-guarded manifest correction changes the invalid one-element library array into a library table; Fortran sources are unchanged. Other I/O modules and malformed-input handling are not covered.

Fixed-width unsigned integer derived types. The main checks 16/32-bit upper boundaries, 32-bit arithmetic above the signed boundary, comparisons, modular addition/subtraction and conversion of a negative assignment. It imports the current int_m conversion API explicitly. This is not arbitrary-precision arithmetic or validation of every kind, operation or C interoperability path.

Functional unit-testing framework. The main runs three specification-style cases checking a small user-written Simpson formula against known constant, linear and quadratic integrals. The numerical formula belongs to the example, not the package. Parallel testing, generators and the complete framework are not validated.

Token-based expression parsing with user-supplied callbacks. The main checks precedence, parentheses, right-associative exponentiation, square root and unary minus against five exact results. A checksum-guarded edit moves a host-independent library callback to module scope after the original layout crashed in the sandbox; parsing rules are unchanged. The author documents global registrations, fixed precedences and missing syntax validation; concurrent parsers and malformed expressions are not supported by this example.

SQLite wrapper with bundled SQLite 3.30.1 C sources. The checked main opens an in-memory database, creates a table, inserts three values, verifies count and average, reaches SQLITE_DONE and closes resources. It does not cover persistent files, concurrent use, transactions or the complete SQLite API. Explicit GitLab-to-GitHub alias pins ISO varying string; no source edits.

Structured error lists and logging. The checked main collects two fatal validation messages, filters one by OUT_OF_BOUNDS, checks counts and diagnostic text, and prints both messages. The pinned compatible Strff 3.1.1 avoids the unavailable exceptional_numbers mirror requested through Strff 4.0. No library source edits. This does not cover all logging levels, filtering operators or concurrent use.

Customizable text tokenization. The checked main uses a module callback to split comma, space and tab-separated fields, verifies all three tokens and checks clearing the list. This is lexical splitting, not expression evaluation. No source edits. Malformed input, every callback combination and token object storage are not covered.

Simple fixed-width integer sets. The checked main verifies duplicate rejection, removal and sorted contents for 32-bit values, and duplicate rejection for a 64-bit value above the 32-bit range. Membership is checked from public data, not a separate membership API. No source edits. Performance, every boundary and all operations are not validated.

Reference-counted resource management. Adapted from the author example: a user type extends sp_smart_pointer_t and implements free. The checked main shares one integer resource, verifies reference counts and shared target, checks no premature cleanup and confirms exactly one cleanup after subroutine return. No source edits. This is not exhaustive compiler finalization conformance testing.

Numerical routines from the RPN calculator, called directly without its interactive interface. The checked main verifies a negative cube root, sinc and sech at zero, beta(2,3), modified Bessel I0 at zero, and integer gcd/lcm against known results. A checksum-guarded manifest correction sets source-form=default so .f and .f90 files use their respective forms. No numerical sources are changed. The tests do not establish accuracy over full argument ranges or validate the complete calculator.

Dedicated GAMS B driver: GCD and LCM checked over nonnegative operands 0..64 against independent divisor/multiple searches. NetCDF4 array and attribute I/O. The checked main writes a 2-by-3 double-precision array with dimension names and a kelvin units attribute, closes the file, reopens and verifies every value and the attribute, then deletes the sandbox file. Native NetCDF and HDF5 development packages and include/library paths are pinned in the build recipe. No source edits. It does not cover every type/rank, compression, slicing or malformed files.

CODATA physical constants. The checked main imports the explicit 2022 edition, computes the energy of a 500 nm photon in joules and electron volts, and compares it with independent decimal reference values. The source modules are pre-generated; no network request or Python generation is needed to use them. No source edits. This is a check of three constants and one calculation, not revalidation of the complete CODATA tables or uncertainty propagation.

Derived types and constructors for multidimensional array bounds. The checked main reconstructs and round-trips bounds [-1:1,4:5], traverses exactly six elements using stored bounds and verifies their sum of 270. No source edits. It does not cover all dimensions, vector/tensor wrappers, empty arrays or invalid bounds. This is an indexing utility, not a numerical solver.

Gauss-Kronrod quadrature-rule generation. A checksum-guarded adapter exposes the original internal procedures as module playground_kronrod, removes the large driver loop and declares app as the library directory; The consumer uses the wrapped module instead of running the original batch drivers. Procedure bodies, constants and precision settings are unchanged. The main generates the symmetric 7-point rule, checks six even polynomial integrals through degree 10 at 40-decimal-place tolerance with MPFUN arithmetic, and prints double-precision summaries. Only the unchanged MPFUN dependency is shared. This is a rule generator, not an adaptive integrator or full validation of every rule/order.

Pure Fortran regular expressions by Edward Higgins, distinct from perazz/fortran-regex already selected under fortran-regex. The main checks matching and nonmatching anchored decimal measurements, matched substring, comma/space splitting and replacement. No source edits or native regex library. Pattern whitespace is ignored unless escaped; the author documents missing capture references and other features, so PCRE compatibility and all patterns are not claimed.

Programmatic Fortran edit descriptors. The main generates and applies integer, character and fixed-decimal real formats, checks exact aligned output, and verifies a zero-padded integer. The registry stdlib dependency is mapped to a pinned Git source and manifest version; compatible stdlib objects are reused. No Fortran source edits. Arrays, complex values, user-defined I/O and every descriptor/control mode are not covered.

Type-erased intrinsic values returned through any_type. The checked main returns an integer, a double-precision real and a character value through one function, retrieves each using its matching type, and checks exact values. No source edits. The author documents undefined results for mismatched type/rank conversions; the example does not validate all ranks, kinds, custom extensions or invalid conversions.

FIFO container using C allocations and byte copies. The main enqueues four 64-bit C-interoperable integers, verifies count and exact retrieval order, frees every popped allocation with C free, checks empty-pop behavior and destroys the queue. No source edits. The implementation uses GNU LOC and raw byte storage; the example makes no portability claim for arbitrary derived types, pointer-owning values, threading or every compiler.

UTF-8 string handling using one array element per encoded Unicode code point. The main verifies a round trip, code point count, substring, search and replacement of accented text, and prints the results. No source edits. Combining marks remain separate code points; grapheme segmentation, normalization and malformed-input handling are not validated.

Serial system_clock and CPU timers. The checked main computes the exact sum of integers 1 through 100000, checks finite nonnegative elapsed times and prints the sum and timings. The root manifest VERSION placeholder is replaced with adapter version 0.0.0; the pinned source commit identifies the actual library. FACE is pinned to an already used revision. No Fortran source edits. MPI/OpenMP timers are not enabled or tested; sandbox timings vary and are not benchmark guarantees.

Assertions for integer scalars and arrays plus approximate real comparison with an explicit tolerance. The main captures an intentional failed comparison as a logical status and message, checks both, and continues successfully. No source edits; matches the existing Any dependency revision. Not a validation of every type, rank, tolerance convention, custom comparator or test-framework integration.

Error status and message handling. A custom reciprocal routine uses catch_error and set_success. The main checks a successful result, zero rejection with an exact code and message, and a subsequent successful call clearing the error. No source edits. The reciprocal is only a driver, not a mathematical procedure supplied by errstat. Optional omitted-status termination and user-defined task/message repositories are not exercised.

Generic singly linked list for small datasets. The main checks integer and real payloads in insertion order, list size, iteration count, emptying, retained capacity and the value stored after reuse; iterator and list cleanup are explicit. A checksum-guarded compatibility edit removes PURE from node_init, whose result has a polymorphic allocatable component. Constructor allocation and copying are unchanged, and the call sites are impure. This patched root retains its own small archive instead of sharing an unmodified graph export. No display dependency is needed for the custom consumer. Large-data performance, all mutation operations and ownership of pointer-containing derived types are not validated.

String enclosure with automatically matched closing brackets and explicit delimiters. The main checks nested bracket reversal, square brackets, quotation marks, custom opening/closing strings and disabled autoclosing, and prints examples. No source edits; matches the existing FED dependency revision. This is formatting, not parsing or escaping untrusted text.

Linear lookup tables. An operator-owned FPM manifest wraps the unchanged m_lookup_table.f90 file. The main checks exact interpolation of a linear function, the expected interpolation error for a quadratic, an exact grid value, and clamping below/above the endpoints. No mathematical source edits. The 2D interface, nonuniform spacing options, persistence and all boundary cases are not validated by this example.

Xoroshiro128+ pseudo-random generator. An FPM wrapper selects unchanged m_random.f90 and uses -fwrapv for its intentional signed-integer wraparound. Two fresh generators replay 10000 seeded uniform draws exactly; the main checks the implementation range [0,1), broad uniform/normal/Poisson(4) moment tolerances, nonnegative counts and unit circle/sphere norms. These are deterministic smoke checks, not statistical quality or cryptographic validation. OpenMP, jump independence, large Poisson rates and all distributions are not covered. A separate hosted reproducer confirms that set_seed does not clear the cached second normal after an odd normal() call; use a fresh generator to restart normal sequences. The selected replay uses fresh objects.

Numeric text parsing. FPM 0.12 rejects the upstream features/profiles tables; a checksum-guarded manifest adaptation removes them and supplies the intended -fno-range-check compiler setting explicitly. The Fortran sources are unchanged and development-only benchmark dependencies are not built. The main checks decimal/scientific and Fortran D-exponent parsing, the largest positive signed int64, hexadecimal parsing, invalid-input status and exponent-overflow status. Correct rounding for every input, all formats, underflow, platforms and speed claims are not validated.

Documented configuration values. An FPM wrapper selects unchanged m_config.f90. The main creates its own tiny configuration file, overrides integer, logical, string and grouped real defaults, reads a dynamically sized real array, checks every value and clears the configuration. No uploaded data file or external service is required. Command-line parsing, invalid-file diagnostics and all string/array/grouping behavior are not validated.

Nearest-neighbor and radius searches. An FPM wrapper selects unchanged src-f90/kdtree2.f90; the archived upstream single-precision setting is retained. The checked main builds a tree for 30 deterministic 2D points, compares four nearest indices and squared distances against an independent direct search, and checks radius-search count, membership, distances and uniqueness. The original Academic Free License 1.1 is retained. No source edits. The implementation has global search state and is not offered as thread-safe; the old interface, C++ code, every dimension and large-scale performance are not validated.

Portable numerical kinds, formats and number/string conversions. The latest archive is blocked by a symlink, so this entry uses exactly the older revision already verified as a BeFoR64 dependency. The checked main calls penf_init, verifies integer and real conversion round trips with status checks, zero-padded integer output, real byte size and formatted real output. Sources are unchanged; this adds an independent editable main for the pinned library. Every kind, character encoding, endian platform and invalid conversion is not validated.

Forward-mode automatic differentiation with dual numbers. The main checks the upstream scalar example against its analytical value and derivative, a two-variable polynomial gradient and a square 2-by-2 Jacobian against exact formulas. GNU heap trampolines support the internal callback procedures in the restricted sandbox. Library sources are unchanged. The author limits jacobian to square problems and documents incomplete intrinsic coverage; sparse interfaces, every overload and all failure modes are not validated.

Scientific utilities. The main sorts repeated and negative integers, builds a k-d tree for 20 deterministic 2D points and compares the nearest point with an independent direct search. The OpenMP metapackage is resolved explicitly and -fopenmp is enabled; the execution sandbox still uses one thread. No source edits. The broad library is compiled, but this driver does not validate all containers, random generators, mathematical utilities or parallel performance.

Scientific utilities. The main sorts repeated and negative integers, builds a k-d tree for 20 deterministic 2D points and compares the nearest point with an independent direct search. The OpenMP metapackage is resolved explicitly and -fopenmp is enabled; the execution sandbox still uses one thread. No source edits. The broad library is compiled, but this driver does not validate all containers, random generators, mathematical utilities or parallel performance.

Version 1 multivariate interpolation using sparse Delaunay simplices. Version 2 bundles BQPD with a research-only redistribution notice, so the selected pin uses the earlier MIT-licensed version 1 with its bundled SLATEC/BLAS/LAPACK sources. An FPM wrapper retains fixed/free source forms, legacy implicit typing/interfaces and -fallow-argument-mismatch for the SLATEC scalar-zero/zero-stride BLAS convention. OpenMP is enabled to link the library; the checked driver uses the serial routine. It verifies exact linear-function reproduction at three interior 2D points, zero status codes, valid simplex indices and barycentric weight sums/signs. No numerical source edits. Convex-hull projection/extrapolation, all degenerate inputs, high-dimensional behavior and parallel variants are not validated.

NumPy NPY writing. An FPM wrapper selects unchanged src/npy.f90. The main writes a 2-by-3 real64 matrix, checks version-2 magic, dtype/order header, exact binary payload and file size, and prints the matrix and header. A separate hosted probe captures the actual file bytes and NumPy independently loads the expected shape, dtype and exact values with pickle disabled. No source edits. The author no longer actively maintains the project. Other kinds/ranks, big-endian platforms and NPZ archive operations are not validated; the browser displays the checked summary rather than offering a general NPY-file download.

procedure_mappings.notes: Selected Fortran Template Library instantiations: integer dynamic arrays and ftlString-to-integer hash maps, plus their unmodified support modules. A checksum-guarded adapter adds CPP-disabled module/dependency declarations so FPM 0.12 can discover modules emitted by templates. Original and adapted compiler-preprocessed output match apart from blank lines. Implicit-external checking is left at the upstream convention to avoid a GNU diagnostic in a character-length specification expression. The checked main verifies array growth, contents and pop, map insertion/replacement, presence, lookup and erase, then explicitly deletes both containers. Sources otherwise remain unchanged, and template headers remain in the source archive. Other instantiations, general algorithms, regex and every ownership/finalization case are not offered or validated.

Serial QNSTOP for bound-constrained stochastic and global optimization. An FPM wrapper selects unmodified REAL_PRECISION, ZIGARRAY, QNSTOPS and bundled BLAS/LAPACK sources. Explicit CPP suffix handling lets FPM discover .f95 files. Legacy implicit typing/interfaces and argument-mismatch compatibility retain the upstream calling conventions. The seeded two-variable quadratic example checks normal stopping status, bounds, objective value and distance from its known minimizer. It is an accuracy smoke test, not a general global-optimum guarantee. The parallel QNSTOPP driver, noisy objectives, all stopping rules and performance are not validated.

Serial FFTW Poisson solvers. An FPM wrapper selects the Fortran library modules, retains upstream template includes, adds CPP-disabled USE declarations for the FPM dependency scanner, declares unused MPI/PFFT modules external for scanning, enables CPP and links Debian FFTW 3.3.10 single/double and thread libraries. MPI/PFFT and C/C++ bindings are not offered. The checked double-precision periodic 1D spectral problem compares its solution with sin(2*pi*x) at 32 points. Other boundary conditions, finite-difference modes, nonuniform grids, higher-dimensional solvers, single precision and parallel execution are not validated.

LMDB key-value database bindings with Debian LMDB 0.9.31. A checksum-guarded compatibility edit selects the existing signed-kind fallback rather than GNU unsigned extension kinds, which are unavailable without enabling nondefault unsigned support. The checked consumer creates a small sandbox-local database, inserts and updates a value, verifies committed reads and rollback after an aborted update, deletes the key and checks MDB_NOTFOUND, then closes and removes both database files. No persistent storage is provided. Large mappings, concurrent writers/readers, all cursor interfaces and other platforms are not validated.

Fortran bindings to Lua 5.4, linked with Debian Lua 5.4.7. The manifest library name lua-5.4 is adapted to Linux lua5.4; library sources are unchanged. Adapted from the upstream in-memory string example, the consumer defines a Lua function, passes an integer from Fortran, checks Lua load/call status and function type, verifies the returned integer and closes the state. External scripts, callbacks from Lua to Fortran, arbitrary Lua modules and all bindings are not validated.

POSIX/SysV bindings on the playground 64-bit Linux/glibc environment. The source library is unchanged. The manifest features/profiles tables are removed for FPM 0.12 compatibility and their Linux preprocessor flag is supplied explicitly. A 13-byte sandbox-local file is created, its size is checked through c_stat, then c_unlink removes it and Fortran INQUIRE confirms removal. Other operating systems, process creation, networking, IPC, signals, threads and all ABI structures are not validated or promised in the restricted sandbox.

Serial derivative-free, bound-constrained multiobjective optimization. An FPM wrapper selects the unchanged solver, surrogate and test-function sources with bundled SLATEC support and links system LP64 BLAS/LAPACK rather than recompiling those bundled libraries. OpenMP linking is enabled, but the checked run uses the serial driver and one execution thread; heap trampolines support internal callbacks in the sandbox. Adapted from the author serial driver and CONVEX function, the seeded 3-variable/2-objective example uses a small evaluation budget, checks feasible design bounds, recomputes both quadratic objectives independently and verifies that no returned point dominates another. It requires multiple distinct trade-off points. This checks the finite returned set, not convergence to the exact global Pareto front or comparative performance. Parallel evaluation, checkpoint recovery, every surrogate and other problem classes are not validated.

procedure_mappings.derivatives: User-supplied analytical state Jacobian in this demo; tangent initial conditions select the rate sensitivity.
procedure_mappings.notes: Selected FATODE explicit Runge-Kutta tangent-linear integrator, linked to native BLAS/LAPACK. The FPM wrapper compiles unchanged TLM/ERK_TLM/ERK_TLM_f90_Integrator.F90; bundled precompiled platform binaries are not used. The example augments exponential decay with a constant rate state and differentiates the initial rate using the tangent-linear model, checking the state, rate, and both sensitivities against analytical formulas. It explicitly selects the supplied analytical Jacobian and enables tangent-variable adaptive error control; the initial default finite-difference Jacobian settings missed the requested sensitivity accuracy. No numerical library edits. Implicit/stiff solvers, adjoint integration, sparse solver variants and all ERK methods are not offered or verified.

Dedicated D8 driver checks continuous/discrete Lyapunov with transpose options and Schur reuse using constructed known solutions, finite outputs, explicit success status and independently recomputed residuals. See docs/gams-matrix-equations.md for equations, storage, scaling and limitations.

Serial classic Fortran ARPACK-NG interfaces, built from unchanged SRC .f files, the documented UTIL support set, and upstream debug/statistics initializers. The wrapper uses native LP64 BLAS/LAPACK and excludes PARPACK/MPI and generated C bindings. The upstream second_NONE timing stub disables ARPACK internal elapsed-time statistics; playground build/run timings still work. Adapted from the author symmetric reverse-communication example, the main computes three smallest eigenpairs of a 20-by-20 symmetric tridiagonal operator, checks convergence status/count, analytical eigenvalues and eigenvector residual norms. A deterministic nonzero initial residual avoids dependence on random initialization. Nonsymmetric/complex modes, shift-invert, generalized problems and parallel execution are not validated. Dedicated D4 driver checks the three smallest and three largest eigenpairs of the 20-by-20 Dirichlet tridiagonal (2 diagonal,-1 off-diagonal), with explicit starting residual, convergence/extraction status, analytical eigenvalues and sign-invariant sine eigenvector comparisons, equation residuals and orthonormality. Generalized, nonsymmetric, shift-invert and arbitrary spectra are not verified. Refined from broad D4 to D4a1 for the reviewed real symmetric ordinary-eigenproblem interfaces.

Structured error handling and validation. The upstream FPM library sources are unchanged; unlimited free-form line length accommodates existing long source lines. Adapted from the author example, the main checks a valid bounded integer in a Result object, rejects an out-of-range integer with expected code 105, checks two retained application trace entries, and triggers a custom noncritical warning while execution continues. The example uses fixed values rather than interactive input. All Result ranks/types, critical-error termination, all validation criteria and every trace-propagation path are not validated.

Runtime assertion checks in pure procedures, built with ASSERTIONS=1 so enforcement is enabled in the cached library. A checksum-guarded manifest edit adds the upstream include directory; library sources and headers are unchanged. The main checks preconditions and postconditions around a pure square-root function. A separate sandbox probe compiles successfully, intentionally calls assert(.false.), and verifies nonzero termination with the expected descriptive diagnostic and unchanged library artifacts, demonstrating that checks were not compiled away. Multi-image/coarray callbacks and every macro variant are not validated. Full current upstream license terms, including its enhancement-contribution provision, are retained under LicenseRef-Berkeley-Assert rather than labeling them as an unmodified standard BSD license.

Native Fortran FMM2D source set selected from the upstream makefile with optional C++ fast kernels disabled. OpenMP and portable -O2 are enabled; the visitor sandbox uses one execution thread and retains bounds checks. Checksum-guarded compatibility edits skip zero-point multipole/local evaluations and zero-source neighbor calls before passing one-past-end array elements. The inverse reorder helper declares its arrays with the actual n extent rather than the legacy dummy extent 1. Source and target branches receive matching guards; formulas are unchanged. The checked real Laplace driver evaluates 512 deterministic sources at 16 separate targets and compares with an independent charge-weighted log-distance sum. A separate source-and-target probe also checks all source potentials by direct summation with self-interactions excluded, exercising the source-side guards. The code is classified as a structured kernel-matrix application and Green-function evaluation related to PDEs, not as a complete boundary-value solver. Helmholtz, biharmonic/Stokes, dipoles, gradients/Hessians, every complex/vector interface and parallel speedups are not validated. The small accuracy check is not a performance benchmark.

Selected unmodified modules types, utils, lapack, mesh, splines and sorting, wrapped for FPM and linked to compatible LP64 BLAS/LAPACK. HDF5, AMOS/special functions, optimization and other unselected modules are not included. The main reproduces a cubic polynomial with the consistent-boundary cubic spline and checks its value, first derivative and second derivative on a denser grid against exact formulas. It checks exponential-mesh endpoints, monotonicity and the requested last/first spacing ratio, then sorts repeated/negative integers against an exact answer. General nonpolynomial interpolation error, extrapolation, every boundary condition, other sorting interfaces and all utility routines are not validated.

Mimetic vector-calculus library with pinned Julienne and Assert dependencies. A single-image coarray build is used. The checked consumer adapts the author's extended Gauss-divergence example to f=x**2/2 and v=x on a 64-cell unit interval. It checks the two volume integrals against 1/3 and 1/6, the boundary flux against 1/2, finiteness and the conservation residual using single-precision tolerances. The command-line parsing and shell display calls of the upstream example are omitted. Library numerical sources are unchanged. Other 2D/3D operators, time integration and convergence orders are not validated. Original Berkeley Lab license terms, including the enhancements clause, are retained; this is not labeled plain BSD-3-Clause.

Unmodified Fortran library sources selected from the upstream native makefile and wrapped for FPM. The checked example adapts the upstream hydrogen test to Z=1 and computes all six (n,l) states through n=3 on an exponential radial mesh. It requires solver convergence, finite energies and agreement with the analytical nonrelativistic energies -1/(2*n**2) within 1e-7 Hartree. Relativistic Dirac, Poisson and self-consistent density-functional calculations are present in the library but not exercised by this example. C/Python bindings and optional extra integration/interpolation/LAPACK sources are outside the selected native source set.

Unmodified mixed C/Fortran POSIX system library in the Linux/glibc sandbox. The checked example creates a local directory with owner-only permissions, writes and reads back the integer 42, checks directory and regular-file types, removes both and confirms cleanup. Other system calls, processes, networking, permissions changes and Windows portability are not validated or promised. Upstream development dependencies and applications are not part of the consumer demonstration.

Fortran/C bindings linked to pinned Debian Tcl/Tk 8.6 development libraries. A checksum-guarded include edit selects Debian's tcl8.6/tcl.h path for the C macro wrappers; interfaces and calculation code are unchanged. Adapted from the upstream evaluation example, the consumer creates a Tcl interpreter, evaluates an in-memory sum-of-squares script, checks evaluation status and the integer result against Fortran, then destroys the interpreter. Tk graphical windows, extension modules, Tcl stubs and all bindings are not validated; the browser example requires no graphical display or network.

Selected base_types, lib_algebra and lib_array modules, using the pinned revision immediately before the upstream FPM test suite introduced source symlinks. Nine checksum-guarded edits bring lib_array exactly to upstream commit 844611933cba06d71490033e68b355f6f0ff704f, retaining its integration-limit, descending histogram-bin and precision fixes. The other selected modules are unchanged. The ordinary archive policy remains unchanged. A synthetic FPM wrapper uses the already generated Fortran sources, not the Python templates. The checked consumer integrates the affine function 2*x+1 on [0,1], checks linear interpolation at an interior off-grid point, and solves x**2-5*x+6 against the exact roots 2 and 3. Additional checks cover integration limits outside the tabulated range, descending histogram bins and bin-center precision; the expanded example fails with the older unpatched array module and passes with the upstream fixes. GAMS F1 denotes the quadratic solver, not a general iterative root finder. Random sampling, statistics, geometry, HDF5/FITS bindings and other modules are not selected; the example does not validate every routine in the included modules.

Pinned Fiats tag 0.12.0 (upstream manifest version 0.11.1), named inference-engine at that revision, with an explicitly pinned compatible Julienne 1.3.1 dependency and Assert 1.7.0. Tag 0.14.0 was tried first but its consumer build cannot find Julienne modules because they are declared only as a development dependency. Single-image coarrays and long free-form lines are enabled. Based on the author's write-read-infer example, the checked consumer constructs a two-input ReLU network with known diagonal weights and biases, evaluates negative, zero and positive input pairs, and compares every output with direct formulas. K is a broad function-approximation classification; training algorithms, gradients, model-file round trips and parallel speedups are not verified. The historical version is explicit in the menu description. The original Berkeley Lab license terms, including the enhancements clause, are retained.

Standalone demonstration of the modern Julienne testing framework, with its pinned Assert dependency and single-image coarrays. The numerical source is unchanged. The checked consumer verifies an approximate real comparison and an exact integer sum, then deliberately creates a failed test_diagnosis_t, checks its failure flag and nonempty appended diagnostic and prints it while completing successfully. This demonstrates diagnosis construction and inspection rather than macro assertion termination. The full test harness, automatic test discovery, macro enforcement and multi-image behavior are not validated. Original Berkeley Lab/Sourcery Institute license terms and dependency notices are retained.

Historical SciPy PROPACK 2.1 sources, whose repository is archived and explicitly points to rmlarsen/propack for the maintained implementation. Its operator FPM wrapper uses version 0.0.0 to identify no inferred upstream release; the source is pinned by commit. The checked main adapts the author integer/string list examples and checks append, insertion, retrieval, successful/missing searches, integer deletion and allocatable-list finalization. N4/N5 cover storage containers and searching. Pointer/array list specializations and the complete upstream tests are not verified. BSD-2-Clause notices are retained.

The original FPM library and Fortran bindings are unchanged. The image pins SDL 2.32.4, SDL2_image 2.8.8, SDL2_mixer 2.8.1, SDL2_ttf 2.24.0 and GL/GLU development libraries; native link flags are recorded in the catalog build environment. The checked main creates a 640x360 32-bit software surface, fills a background and three bars, checks source pixels, saves a PNG, reloads it through the package IMG_Load API, and checks dimensions plus the file signature/size. The pinned bindings omit IMG_SavePNG, so the main includes only that standard C function declaration. No image encoder or drawing algorithm is substituted for SDL. No video subsystem, window, display server, hardware renderer, audio device or event loop is needed. The returned browser preview is visually reviewed. Q covers graphics. Interactive rendering, audio, fonts and OpenGL/GLU routines are compiled/linked facilities but not runtime-verified by this consumer. ISC notices are retained.

Adaptive one-dimensional integration on a finite interval using subdivision and extrapolation for integrable singularities. The checked driver adapts author test_qags (1/sqrt(x)) and adds log(x)/sqrt(x). These endpoint singularities have exact integrals 2 and -4. It checks status zero, finite values, independent accuracy and callback counts; it does not evaluate the singular endpoint or claim coverage of all special integrands.

Real unconstrained linear least squares using the SVD-based GELSD implementation, including rank-deficient minimum-norm solutions.
One-dimensional DCT-II and its inverse. This FFTPACK API uses a forward factor of 4 and an unnormalized inverse; divide the composition by 4*N.

procedure_mappings.notes: Smooth bound-constrained optimization with a user gradient. Explicit lower/upper bounds are part of this configuration, distinct from the unconstrained driver.

Lower-level real64 LAPACK gesvd interface with explicit workspace; high-level wrapper is a separate configuration.
Real64 variance with explicit corrected=.true. (sample) or .false. (population); masked subsets and dimension reduction are demonstrated.

Jenkins-Traub all-roots solver for real polynomial coefficients. The checked F1a driver checks distinct known roots without relying on output order, normalized Horner residuals, and coefficient scales 1, 1e80 and 1e-80. Repeated or tightly clustered roots, extreme degree and all invalid inputs are outside this validation.

The checked F1a driver checks distinct known roots without relying on output order, normalized Horner residuals, and coefficient scales 1, 1e80 and 1e-80. Repeated or tightly clustered roots, extreme degree and all invalid inputs are outside this validation.

review_notes.stdlib: Selected subclasses cover documented linear algebra, summary statistics, random numbers, strings, containers, sorting and error handling. A and C remain broad pending a pinned-routine inventory.
review_notes.fortran_function_parser: N3 covers expression text processing. C remains broad; this review does not inventory each supported mathematical function.
review_notes.m_calculator: N3 covers expression text processing. C remains broad pending an inventory of built-in functions; numeric evaluation is not symbolic algebra.
review_notes.kinds: A and R remain broad: precision-kind declarations alone do not establish arithmetic algorithms or a machine-constant API.
review_notes.datetime-fortran: R has no immediate date/time subclass. Calendar services retain the parent assignment.
review_notes.m_time: R has no immediate date/time subclass. Calendar services retain the parent assignment.
review_notes.functional-fortran: N4 covers array/container operations. The general programming support remains at S rather than claiming transformation or analysis tools.
review_notes.popen-fortran: N1 covers captured process output. Process support remains at S; no immediate analysis-tool subclass is claimed.
review_notes.quaff: Dimensioned arithmetic and unit conversion retain A/Z. No immediate arithmetic subtype is claimed without reviewing the representation-specific API.
review_notes.metis-fpm: Sparse-matrix ordering remains at D and graph partitioning at P; this is not a linear-system solver assignment.
review_notes.forpca: D4 and D6 describe the eigenvalue/SVD methods. PCA retains the parent L assignment rather than guessing an immediate statistical subclass.
review_notes.neural-fortran: G1 covers gradient-based network training. K remains broad because the package is not restricted to least-squares fitting.
review_notes.spectrum: J1/J2 cover transforms and convolution, K5 smoothing. General signal-data handling retains N without claiming a specific data-management operation.
review_notes.fmin: G1 denotes scalar minimization using a finite search interval; it does not claim support for general nonlinear constraints.
review_notes.powellopt: G2 is supported by BOBYQA bound constraints and COBYLA constraints. No unconstrained subclass is inferred solely from the Powell family name.
review_notes.fstats: Distribution evaluation, random sampling, summaries, statistical tests, resampling, regression and MCMC support the selected statistical and simulation subclasses.
review_notes.daskr: I1 includes the package's ordinary differential-algebraic systems; this assignment does not claim PDE or integral-equation solvers.
review_notes.diffeq: I1 includes both the ordinary differential and differential-algebraic integrators.
review_notes.m_la: Matrix construction, illustrated by magic squares of orders three through six with independent row, column, diagonal and permutation checks. This mapping does not classify every other M_LA procedure.
review_notes.fglm: Vector addition and component products, and column-major homogeneous translation and rotation matrices. The example checks a known point and a quarter-turn about z; broader geometry functionality is not exhaustively validated.
review_notes.fortrandf: Named heterogeneous in-memory columns; retrieval and a calibration update are checked. This is a storage example, not a statistical estimation library.
review_notes.strith: Signed decimal-string integer addition and subtraction beyond 64-bit range, plus unsigned interpretation of an int64 bit pattern. This is fixed-capacity decimal representation, not unlimited arbitrary precision.
review_notes.list: Linked-list storage, lookup, duplicate counts, sorting, removal and clearing; the demo uses a module comparator.
review_notes.friction: Constitutive friction models, with nonlinear parameter fitting and internal-state ODE integration in the reviewed source. The checked main covers algebraic Coulomb and Stribeck forces only; it does not validate parameter fitting or dynamic internal-state integration.
review_notes.feq-parse: Numerical evaluation of expressions parsed from text, not symbolic algebra. The demo checks double-precision multivariable Gaussian and polynomial expressions against direct Fortran formulas.
review_notes.fordot: Scalar products using methods m1 through m4, each also checked with three unequal blocks against an exact answer. Single-process correctness only; no coarray or performance claim.
review_notes.formatmul: Methods m1 through m4 are checked for rectangular matrix multiplication, all transpose combinations and a matrix-vector product. The demo is single-process and does not validate every implementation or coarray branch. At this pin a single explicitly false transpose flag is misrouted; the demo passes both flags whenever either is specified. Separate failing probes and the successful workaround are retained.
review_notes.bstrith: Fixed-width binary-string addition, subtraction, shifts and logical operations. The driver checks every eight-bit value, including carry and wraparound. This is not unlimited arbitrary-precision arithmetic.
review_notes.heatflow: Fourier/Cattaneo heat-transport code. The checked main applies its sparse BiCG solver to an independent backward-Euler discretization of the one-dimensional heat equation; it checks the discrete solution, continuous-solution error and independent matrix residuals. It does not exercise the complete evolution/Cattaneo application.
review_notes.hrweno: WENO spatial reconstruction and explicit TVD Runge-Kutta integration for conservation equations. The main checks a smooth periodic advection problem against exact cell averages and verifies conservation of mass; discontinuous solutions and nonuniform grids are not covered.
review_notes.fortran-simplify: Polyline simplification. The main checks one call of perpendicular-distance reduction against endpoints and an independent interpolation bound, and plots the original and reduced curves. Separate GNU 16 probes confirm incorrect radial-distance filtering and lost endpoints on consecutive perpendicular-distance calls at this pin; see the retained reproducers. The single-call example does not fix those upstream limitations.
review_notes.ecx: Electrochemical models with complex-valued equivalent-circuit impedance. The main verifies resistor and capacitor impedances and their series combination against direct complex formulas at four angular frequencies. Kinetics and parameter estimation are not covered. A4 classifies the complex arithmetic interface, not an electrochemistry-specific GAMS class.
review_notes.athena: Neural-network function approximation. A fixed-weight dense layer with tanh activation is compared against direct Fortran matrix multiplication and TANH. This does not test training, automatic derivatives, graph convolutions or model accuracy on a dataset. K remains broad.
review_notes.orbs: Fixed-width bitset arithmetic and logical operations. The main computes an x neighbor for every cell of a two-dimensional 4-by-4 Morton grid, checking all sixteen results and wraparound against independent intrinsic integer operations.
review_notes.rearrayfx: Growable real rank-two arrays backed by spare capacity. The main checks data preservation across growth within spare capacity, reallocation, shrinking and plain-array assignment. This proof of concept is not a general-purpose container or a test of copying between container instances.
review_notes.amosf90: AMOS module interfaces for complex-argument Bessel functions with noninteger nonnegative order, including modified Bessel functions. The checked main compares J_0.3 and I_0.3 at 1+0.5i with independent convergent power series and K_0.5 with its closed form. Other argument regions, orders, scaling modes and Airy/Hankel routines are not validated. The upstream README warns of possible bugs.
review_notes.linalg_fortran: Typed LAPACK interfaces. The checked real64 main verifies a matrix inverse residual, determinant, known eigenvalues, eigenpair residuals and orthonormality for a symmetric 3-by-3 tridiagonal matrix. Complex, single-precision and other BLAS/LAPACK wrappers are not covered. Legacy implicit external interfaces are explicitly enabled in the pinned package manifest.
review_notes.fortran_vector: Growable integer vectors. The checked main verifies growth from a two-element capacity, appended arrays, stable duplicate removal, remove/delete/pop and final compaction against independent expected contents. A checksum-guarded one-line edit fixes aliasing in unique: remove the already saved first value instead of the first array element while that array is being compacted. Empty-vector unique and all invalid-input cases are not covered.
review_notes.scanner: Character-by-character text scanning. The main reconstructs a configuration record through current/next, verifies navigation and end boundaries, and checks that peek does not move the cursor. The recovered fields are converted with ordinary internal READ and compared with known values; this is a small parser example, not a full parsing language.
review_notes.rojff: JSON parsing and serialization with explicit error values. The main checks numeric/string fields, missing-key reporting, compact serialization round trips and malformed-input rejection. It uses the original Erloff 2.2.0 API with a pinned compatible Strff 3.1.1 and ISO varying string 3.0.3; the Strff 4.0 dependency graph needs an unavailable GitHub mirror. No computational source is patched.
review_notes.argparse-f: Typed process command-line parsing. The main launches itself once with fixed example arguments, then checks an integer, double, string, logical flag and untouched default. No supplied files or playground argument-setting changes are needed. Error exits, positional/named arguments, truncation and every syntax variant are not covered.
review_notes.io_utilities: Key/value configuration input. The main creates and reads a tiny INI-style file with a section, comment, integer, double, logical and string, verifies known values and deletes it. A checksum-guarded manifest correction changes the invalid one-element library array into a library table; Fortran sources are unchanged. Other I/O modules and malformed-input handling are not covered.
review_notes.uint-fortran: Fixed-width unsigned integer derived types. The main checks 16/32-bit upper boundaries, 32-bit arithmetic above the signed boundary, comparisons, modular addition/subtraction and conversion of a negative assignment. It imports the current int_m conversion API explicitly. This is not arbitrary-precision arithmetic or validation of every kind, operation or C interoperability path.
review_notes.veggies: Functional unit-testing framework. The main runs three specification-style cases checking a small user-written Simpson formula against known constant, linear and quadratic integrals. The numerical formula belongs to the example, not the package. Parallel testing, generators and the complete framework are not validated.
review_notes.shunting-yard-fortran: Token-based expression parsing with user-supplied callbacks. The main checks precedence, parentheses, right-associative exponentiation, square root and unary minus against five exact results. A checksum-guarded edit moves a host-independent library callback to module scope after the original layout crashed in the sandbox; parsing rules are unchanged. The author documents global registrations, fixed precedences and missing syntax validation; concurrent parsers and malformed expressions are not supported by this example.
review_notes.sqliteff: SQLite wrapper with bundled SQLite 3.30.1 C sources. The checked main opens an in-memory database, creates a table, inserts three values, verifies count and average, reaches SQLITE_DONE and closes resources. It does not cover persistent files, concurrent use, transactions or the complete SQLite API. Explicit GitLab-to-GitHub alias pins ISO varying string; no source edits.
review_notes.erloff: Structured error lists and logging. The checked main collects two fatal validation messages, filters one by OUT_OF_BOUNDS, checks counts and diagnostic text, and prints both messages. The pinned compatible Strff 3.1.1 avoids the unavailable exceptional_numbers mirror requested through Strff 4.0. No library source edits. This does not cover all logging levels, filtering operators or concurrent use.
review_notes.fortran-tokenizer: Customizable text tokenization. The checked main uses a module callback to split comma, space and tab-separated fields, verifies all three tokens and checks clearing the list. This is lexical splitting, not expression evaluation. No source edits. Malformed input, every callback combination and token object storage are not covered.
review_notes.integer_set: Simple fixed-width integer sets. The checked main verifies duplicate rejection, removal and sorted contents for 32-bit values, and duplicate rejection for a 64-bit value above the 32-bit range. Membership is checked from public data, not a separate membership API. No source edits. Performance, every boundary and all operations are not validated.
review_notes.smart-pointers: Reference-counted resource management. Adapted from the author example: a user type extends sp_smart_pointer_t and implements free. The checked main shares one integer resource, verifies reference counts and shared target, checks no premature cleanup and confirms exactly one cleanup after subroutine return. No source edits. This is not exhaustive compiler finalization conformance testing.
review_notes.rpn-calculator-fortran: Numerical routines from the RPN calculator, called directly without its interactive interface. The checked main verifies a negative cube root, sinc and sech at zero, beta(2,3), modified Bessel I0 at zero, and integer gcd/lcm against known results. A checksum-guarded manifest correction sets source-form=default so .f and .f90 files use their respective forms. No numerical sources are changed. The tests do not establish accuracy over full argument ranges or validate the complete calculator.
review_notes.nc4fortran: NetCDF4 array and attribute I/O. The checked main writes a 2-by-3 double-precision array with dimension names and a kelvin units attribute, closes the file, reopens and verifies every value and the attribute, then deletes the sandbox file. Native NetCDF and HDF5 development packages and include/library paths are pinned in the build recipe. No source edits. It does not cover every type/rank, compression, slicing or malformed files.
review_notes.fundamental_constants: CODATA physical constants. The checked main imports the explicit 2022 edition, computes the energy of a 500 nm photon in joules and electron volts, and compares it with independent decimal reference values. The source modules are pre-generated; no network request or Python generation is needed to use them. No source edits. This is a check of three constants and one calculation, not revalidation of the complete CODATA tables or uncertainty propagation.
review_notes.array_range: Derived types and constructors for multidimensional array bounds. The checked main reconstructs and round-trips bounds [-1:1,4:5], traverses exactly six elements using stored bounds and verifies their sum of 270. No source edits. It does not cover all dimensions, vector/tensor wrappers, empty arrays or invalid bounds. This is an indexing utility, not a numerical solver.
review_notes.kronrod: Gauss-Kronrod quadrature-rule generation. A checksum-guarded adapter exposes the original internal procedures as module playground_kronrod, removes the large driver loop and declares app as the library directory; The consumer uses the wrapped module instead of running the original batch drivers. Procedure bodies, constants and precision settings are unchanged. The main generates the symmetric 7-point rule, checks six even polynomial integrals through degree 10 at 40-decimal-place tolerance with MPFUN arithmetic, and prints double-precision summaries. Only the unchanged MPFUN dependency is shared. This is a rule generator, not an adaptive integrator or full validation of every rule/order.
review_notes.jeyemhex-regex: Pure Fortran regular expressions by Edward Higgins, distinct from perazz/fortran-regex already selected under fortran-regex. The main checks matching and nonmatching anchored decimal measurements, matched substring, comma/space splitting and replacement. No source edits or native regex library. Pattern whitespace is ignored unless escaped; the author documents missing capture references and other features, so PCRE compatibility and all patterns are not claimed.
review_notes.fed: Programmatic Fortran edit descriptors. The main generates and applies integer, character and fixed-decimal real formats, checks exact aligned output, and verifies a zero-padded integer. The registry stdlib dependency is mapped to a pinned Git source and manifest version; compatible stdlib objects are reused. No Fortran source edits. Arrays, complex values, user-defined I/O and every descriptor/control mode are not covered.
review_notes.any: Type-erased intrinsic values returned through any_type. The checked main returns an integer, a double-precision real and a character value through one function, retrieves each using its matching type, and checks exact values. No source edits. The author documents undefined results for mismatched type/rank conversions; the example does not validate all ranks, kinds, custom extensions or invalid conversions.
review_notes.for_fifo_queue: FIFO container using C allocations and byte copies. The main enqueues four 64-bit C-interoperable integers, verifies count and exact retrieval order, frees every popped allocation with C free, checks empty-pop behavior and destroys the queue. No source edits. The implementation uses GNU LOC and raw byte storage; the example makes no portability claim for arbitrary derived types, pointer-owning values, threading or every compiler.
review_notes.string-utf-8: UTF-8 string handling using one array element per encoded Unicode code point. The main verifies a round trip, code point count, substring, search and replacement of accented text, and prints the results. No source edits. Combining marks remain separate code points; grapheme segmentation, normalization and malformed-input handling are not validated.
review_notes.fortime: Serial system_clock and CPU timers. The checked main computes the exact sum of integers 1 through 100000, checks finite nonnegative elapsed times and prints the sum and timings. The root manifest VERSION placeholder is replaced with adapter version 0.0.0; the pinned source commit identifies the actual library. FACE is pinned to an already used revision. No Fortran source edits. MPI/OpenMP timers are not enabled or tested; sandbox timings vary and are not benchmark guarantees.
review_notes.fassert: Assertions for integer scalars and arrays plus approximate real comparison with an explicit tolerance. The main captures an intentional failed comparison as a logical status and message, checks both, and continues successfully. No source edits; matches the existing Any dependency revision. Not a validation of every type, rank, tolerance convention, custom comparator or test-framework integration.
review_notes.errstat: Error status and message handling. A custom reciprocal routine uses catch_error and set_success. The main checks a successful result, zero rejection with an exact code and message, and a subsequent successful call clearing the error. No source edits. The reciprocal is only a driver, not a mathematical procedure supplied by errstat. Optional omitted-status termination and user-defined task/message repositories are not exercised.
review_notes.slinked-list: Generic singly linked list for small datasets. The main checks integer and real payloads in insertion order, list size, iteration count, emptying, retained capacity and the value stored after reuse; iterator and list cleanup are explicit. A checksum-guarded compatibility edit removes PURE from node_init, whose result has a polymorphic allocatable component. Constructor allocation and copying are unchanged, and the call sites are impure. This patched root retains its own small archive instead of sharing an unmodified graph export. No display dependency is needed for the custom consumer. Large-data performance, all mutation operations and ownership of pointer-containing derived types are not validated.
review_notes.enclose: String enclosure with automatically matched closing brackets and explicit delimiters. The main checks nested bracket reversal, square brackets, quotation marks, custom opening/closing strings and disabled autoclosing, and prints examples. No source edits; matches the existing FED dependency revision. This is formatting, not parsing or escaping untrusted text.
review_notes.lookup-table-fortran: Linear lookup tables. An operator-owned FPM manifest wraps the unchanged m_lookup_table.f90 file. The main checks exact interpolation of a linear function, the expected interpolation error for a quadratic, an exact grid value, and clamping below/above the endpoints. No mathematical source edits. The 2D interface, nonuniform spacing options, persistence and all boundary cases are not validated by this example.
review_notes.rng-fortran: Xoroshiro128+ pseudo-random generator. An FPM wrapper selects unchanged m_random.f90 and uses -fwrapv for its intentional signed-integer wraparound. Two fresh generators replay 10000 seeded uniform draws exactly; the main checks the implementation range [0,1), broad uniform/normal/Poisson(4) moment tolerances, nonnegative counts and unit circle/sphere norms. These are deterministic smoke checks, not statistical quality or cryptographic validation. OpenMP, jump independence, large Poisson rates and all distributions are not covered. A separate hosted reproducer confirms that set_seed does not clear the cached second normal after an odd normal() call; use a fresh generator to restart normal sequences. The selected replay uses fresh objects.
review_notes.fortran-fast-float: Numeric text parsing. FPM 0.12 rejects the upstream features/profiles tables; a checksum-guarded manifest adaptation removes them and supplies the intended -fno-range-check compiler setting explicitly. The Fortran sources are unchanged and development-only benchmark dependencies are not built. The main checks decimal/scientific and Fortran D-exponent parsing, the largest positive signed int64, hexadecimal parsing, invalid-input status and exponent-overflow status. Correct rounding for every input, all formats, underflow, platforms and speed claims are not validated.
review_notes.config-fortran: Documented configuration values. An FPM wrapper selects unchanged m_config.f90. The main creates its own tiny configuration file, overrides integer, logical, string and grouped real defaults, reads a dynamically sized real array, checks every value and clears the configuration. No uploaded data file or external service is required. Command-line parsing, invalid-file diagnostics and all string/array/grouping behavior are not validated.
review_notes.kdtree2: Nearest-neighbor and radius searches. An FPM wrapper selects unchanged src-f90/kdtree2.f90; the archived upstream single-precision setting is retained. The checked main builds a tree for 30 deterministic 2D points, compares four nearest indices and squared distances against an independent direct search, and checks radius-search count, membership, distances and uniqueness. The original Academic Free License 1.1 is retained. No source edits. The implementation has global search state and is not offered as thread-safe; the old interface, C++ code, every dimension and large-scale performance are not validated.
review_notes.penf: Portable numerical kinds, formats and number/string conversions. The latest archive is blocked by a symlink, so this entry uses exactly the older revision already verified as a BeFoR64 dependency. The checked main calls penf_init, verifies integer and real conversion round trips with status checks, zero-padded integer output, real byte size and formatted real output. Sources are unchanged; this adds an independent editable main for the pinned library. Every kind, character encoding, endian platform and invalid conversion is not validated.
review_notes.differentia: Forward-mode automatic differentiation with dual numbers. The main checks the upstream scalar example against its analytical value and derivative, a two-variable polynomial gradient and a square 2-by-2 Jacobian against exact formulas. GNU heap trampolines support the internal callback procedures in the restricted sandbox. Library sources are unchanged. The author limits jacobian to square problems and documents incomplete intrinsic coverage; sparse interfaces, every overload and all failure modes are not validated.
review_notes.coretran: Scientific utilities. The main sorts repeated and negative integers, builds a k-d tree for 20 deterministic 2D points and compares the nearest point with an independent direct search. The OpenMP metapackage is resolved explicitly and -fopenmp is enabled; the execution sandbox still uses one thread. No source edits. The broad library is compiled, but this driver does not validate all containers, random generators, mathematical utilities or parallel performance.
review_notes.delaunaysparse: Version 1 multivariate interpolation using sparse Delaunay simplices. Version 2 bundles BQPD with a research-only redistribution notice, so the selected pin uses the earlier MIT-licensed version 1 with its bundled SLATEC/BLAS/LAPACK sources. An FPM wrapper retains fixed/free source forms, legacy implicit typing/interfaces and -fallow-argument-mismatch for the SLATEC scalar-zero/zero-stride BLAS convention. OpenMP is enabled to link the library; the checked driver uses the serial routine. It verifies exact linear-function reproduction at three interior 2D points, zero status codes, valid simplex indices and barycentric weight sums/signs. No numerical source edits. Convex-hull projection/extrapolation, all degenerate inputs, high-dimensional behavior and parallel variants are not validated.
review_notes.npy-for-fortran: NumPy NPY writing. An FPM wrapper selects unchanged src/npy.f90. The main writes a 2-by-3 real64 matrix, checks version-2 magic, dtype/order header, exact binary payload and file size, and prints the matrix and header. A separate hosted probe captures the actual file bytes and NumPy independently loads the expected shape, dtype and exact values with pickle disabled. No source edits. The author no longer actively maintains the project. Other kinds/ranks, big-endian platforms and NPZ archive operations are not validated; the browser displays the checked summary rather than offering a general NPY-file download.
review_notes.ftl: Selected Fortran Template Library instantiations: integer dynamic arrays and ftlString-to-integer hash maps, plus their unmodified support modules. A checksum-guarded adapter adds CPP-disabled module/dependency declarations so FPM 0.12 can discover modules emitted by templates. Original and adapted compiler-preprocessed output match apart from blank lines. Implicit-external checking is left at the upstream convention to avoid a GNU diagnostic in a character-length specification expression. The checked main verifies array growth, contents and pop, map insertion/replacement, presence, lookup and erase, then explicitly deletes both containers. Sources otherwise remain unchanged, and template headers remain in the source archive. Other instantiations, general algorithms, regex and every ownership/finalization case are not offered or validated.
review_notes.qnstop: Serial QNSTOP for bound-constrained stochastic and global optimization. An FPM wrapper selects unmodified REAL_PRECISION, ZIGARRAY, QNSTOPS and bundled BLAS/LAPACK sources. Explicit CPP suffix handling lets FPM discover .f95 files. Legacy implicit typing/interfaces and argument-mismatch compatibility retain the upstream calling conventions. The seeded two-variable quadratic example checks normal stopping status, bounds, objective value and distance from its known minimizer. It is an accuracy smoke test, not a general global-optimum guarantee. The parallel QNSTOPP driver, noisy objectives, all stopping rules and performance are not validated.
review_notes.poisfft: Serial FFTW Poisson solvers. An FPM wrapper selects the Fortran library modules, retains upstream template includes, adds CPP-disabled USE declarations for the FPM dependency scanner, declares unused MPI/PFFT modules external for scanning, enables CPP and links Debian FFTW 3.3.10 single/double and thread libraries. MPI/PFFT and C/C++ bindings are not offered. The checked double-precision periodic 1D spectral problem compares its solution with sin(2*pi*x) at 32 points. Other boundary conditions, finite-difference modes, nonuniform grids, higher-dimensional solvers, single precision and parallel execution are not validated.
review_notes.fortran-lmdb: LMDB key-value database bindings with Debian LMDB 0.9.31. A checksum-guarded compatibility edit selects the existing signed-kind fallback rather than GNU unsigned extension kinds, which are unavailable without enabling nondefault unsigned support. The checked consumer creates a small sandbox-local database, inserts and updates a value, verifies committed reads and rollback after an aborted update, deletes the key and checks MDB_NOTFOUND, then closes and removes both database files. No persistent storage is provided. Large mappings, concurrent writers/readers, all cursor interfaces and other platforms are not validated.
review_notes.fortran-lua54: Fortran bindings to Lua 5.4, linked with Debian Lua 5.4.7. The manifest library name lua-5.4 is adapted to Linux lua5.4; library sources are unchanged. Adapted from the upstream in-memory string example, the consumer defines a Lua function, passes an integer from Fortran, checks Lua load/call status and function type, verifies the returned integer and closes the state. External scripts, callbacks from Lua to Fortran, arbitrary Lua modules and all bindings are not validated.
review_notes.fortran-unix: POSIX/SysV bindings on the playground 64-bit Linux/glibc environment. The source library is unchanged. The manifest features/profiles tables are removed for FPM 0.12 compatibility and their Linux preprocessor flag is supplied explicitly. A 13-byte sandbox-local file is created, its size is checked through c_stat, then c_unlink removes it and Fortran INQUIRE confirms removal. Other operating systems, process creation, networking, IPC, signals, threads and all ABI structures are not validated or promised in the restricted sandbox.
review_notes.vtmop: Serial derivative-free, bound-constrained multiobjective optimization. An FPM wrapper selects the unchanged solver, surrogate and test-function sources with bundled SLATEC support and links system LP64 BLAS/LAPACK rather than recompiling those bundled libraries. OpenMP linking is enabled, but the checked run uses the serial driver and one execution thread; heap trampolines support internal callbacks in the sandbox. Adapted from the author serial driver and CONVEX function, the seeded 3-variable/2-objective example uses a small evaluation budget, checks feasible design bounds, recomputes both quadratic objectives independently and verifies that no returned point dominates another. It requires multiple distinct trade-off points. This checks the finite returned set, not convergence to the exact global Pareto front or comparative performance. Parallel evaluation, checkpoint recovery, every surrogate and other problem classes are not validated.
review_notes.fatode: Selected FATODE explicit Runge-Kutta tangent-linear integrator, linked to native BLAS/LAPACK. The FPM wrapper compiles unchanged TLM/ERK_TLM/ERK_TLM_f90_Integrator.F90; bundled precompiled platform binaries are not used. The example augments exponential decay with a constant rate state and differentiates the initial rate using the tangent-linear model, checking the state, rate, and both sensitivities against analytical formulas. It explicitly selects the supplied analytical Jacobian and enables tangent-variable adaptive error control; the initial default finite-difference Jacobian settings missed the requested sensitivity accuracy. No numerical library edits. Implicit/stiff solvers, adjoint integration, sparse solver variants and all ERK methods are not offered or verified.
review_notes.slicot: Full upstream SLICOT FPM source library, linked to compatible LP64 BLAS/LAPACK with the manifest BLAS metapackage resolved explicitly. Sources are unchanged; legacy compiler compatibility flags retain upstream conventions. The main uses the author slicot module interface for SB03MD, constructs a stable nondiagonal 2-by-2 continuous Lyapunov problem from a known symmetric solution and checks both the independently computed matrix residual and the recovered solution including the solver scale factor. It requests the condition/error estimates but does not validate those estimates independently. Other matrix equations, model reduction, identification, robust control and every library routine are not validated.
review_notes.arpack-ng: Serial classic Fortran ARPACK-NG interfaces, built from unchanged SRC .f files, the documented UTIL support set, and upstream debug/statistics initializers. The wrapper uses native LP64 BLAS/LAPACK and excludes PARPACK/MPI and generated C bindings. The upstream second_NONE timing stub disables ARPACK internal elapsed-time statistics; playground build/run timings still work. Adapted from the author symmetric reverse-communication example, the main computes three smallest eigenpairs of a 20-by-20 symmetric tridiagonal operator, checks convergence status/count, analytical eigenvalues and eigenvector residual norms. A deterministic nonzero initial residual avoids dependence on random initialization. Nonsymmetric/complex modes, shift-invert, generalized problems and parallel execution are not validated.
review_notes.fortran-error-handler: Structured error handling and validation. The upstream FPM library sources are unchanged; unlimited free-form line length accommodates existing long source lines. Adapted from the author example, the main checks a valid bounded integer in a Result object, rejects an out-of-range integer with expected code 105, checks two retained application trace entries, and triggers a custom noncritical warning while execution continues. The example uses fixed values rather than interactive input. All Result ranks/types, critical-error termination, all validation criteria and every trace-propagation path are not validated.
review_notes.berkeley-assert: Runtime assertion checks in pure procedures, built with ASSERTIONS=1 so enforcement is enabled in the cached library. A checksum-guarded manifest edit adds the upstream include directory; library sources and headers are unchanged. The main checks preconditions and postconditions around a pure square-root function. A separate sandbox probe compiles successfully, intentionally calls assert(.false.), and verifies nonzero termination with the expected descriptive diagnostic and unchanged library artifacts, demonstrating that checks were not compiled away. Multi-image/coarray callbacks and every macro variant are not validated. Full current upstream license terms, including its enhancement-contribution provision, are retained under LicenseRef-Berkeley-Assert rather than labeling them as an unmodified standard BSD license.
review_notes.fmm2d: Native Fortran FMM2D source set selected from the upstream makefile with optional C++ fast kernels disabled. OpenMP and portable -O2 are enabled; the visitor sandbox uses one execution thread and retains bounds checks. Checksum-guarded compatibility edits skip zero-point multipole/local evaluations and zero-source neighbor calls before passing one-past-end array elements. The inverse reorder helper declares its arrays with the actual n extent rather than the legacy dummy extent 1. Source and target branches receive matching guards; formulas are unchanged. The checked real Laplace driver evaluates 512 deterministic sources at 16 separate targets and compares with an independent charge-weighted log-distance sum. A separate source-and-target probe also checks all source potentials by direct summation with self-interactions excluded, exercising the source-side guards. The code is classified as a structured kernel-matrix application and Green-function evaluation related to PDEs, not as a complete boundary-value solver. Helmholtz, biharmonic/Stokes, dipoles, gradients/Hessians, every complex/vector interface and parallel speedups are not validated. The small accuracy check is not a performance benchmark.
review_notes.fortran-utils: Selected unmodified modules types, utils, lapack, mesh, splines and sorting, wrapped for FPM and linked to compatible LP64 BLAS/LAPACK. HDF5, AMOS/special functions, optimization and other unselected modules are not included. The main reproduces a cubic polynomial with the consistent-boundary cubic spline and checks its value, first derivative and second derivative on a denser grid against exact formulas. It checks exponential-mesh endpoints, monotonicity and the requested last/first spacing ratio, then sorts repeated/negative integers against an exact answer. General nonpolynomial interpolation error, extrapolation, every boundary condition, other sorting interfaces and all utility routines are not validated.
review_notes.formal: Mimetic vector-calculus library with pinned Julienne and Assert dependencies. A single-image coarray build is used. The checked consumer adapts the author's extended Gauss-divergence example to f=x**2/2 and v=x on a 64-cell unit interval. It checks the two volume integrals against 1/3 and 1/6, the boundary flux against 1/2, finiteness and the conservation residual using single-precision tolerances. The command-line parsing and shell display calls of the upstream example are omitted. Library numerical sources are unchanged. Other 2D/3D operators, time integration and convergence orders are not validated. Original Berkeley Lab license terms, including the enhancements clause, are retained; this is not labeled plain BSD-3-Clause.
review_notes.dftatom: Unmodified Fortran library sources selected from the upstream native makefile and wrapped for FPM. The checked example adapts the upstream hydrogen test to Z=1 and computes all six (n,l) states through n=3 on an exponential radial mesh. It requires solver convergence, finite energies and agreement with the analytical nonrelativistic energies -1/(2*n**2) within 1e-7 Hartree. Relativistic Dirac, Poisson and self-consistent density-functional calculations are present in the library but not exercised by this example. C/Python bindings and optional extra integration/interpolation/LAPACK sources are outside the selected native source set.
review_notes.m-system: Unmodified mixed C/Fortran POSIX system library in the Linux/glibc sandbox. The checked example creates a local directory with owner-only permissions, writes and reads back the integer 42, checks directory and regular-file types, removes both and confirms cleanup. Other system calls, processes, networking, permissions changes and Windows portability are not validated or promised. Upstream development dependencies and applications are not part of the consumer demonstration.
review_notes.fortran-tcl86: Fortran/C bindings linked to pinned Debian Tcl/Tk 8.6 development libraries. A checksum-guarded include edit selects Debian's tcl8.6/tcl.h path for the C macro wrappers; interfaces and calculation code are unchanged. Adapted from the upstream evaluation example, the consumer creates a Tcl interpreter, evaluates an in-memory sum-of-squares script, checks evaluation status and the integer result against Fortran, then destroys the interpreter. Tk graphical windows, extension modules, Tcl stubs and all bindings are not validated; the browser example requires no graphical display or network.
review_notes.fortranlib: Selected base_types, lib_algebra and lib_array modules, using the pinned revision immediately before the upstream FPM test suite introduced source symlinks. Nine checksum-guarded edits bring lib_array exactly to upstream commit 844611933cba06d71490033e68b355f6f0ff704f, retaining its integration-limit, descending histogram-bin and precision fixes. The other selected modules are unchanged. The ordinary archive policy remains unchanged. A synthetic FPM wrapper uses the already generated Fortran sources, not the Python templates. The checked consumer integrates the affine function 2*x+1 on [0,1], checks linear interpolation at an interior off-grid point, and solves x**2-5*x+6 against the exact roots 2 and 3. Additional checks cover integration limits outside the tabulated range, descending histogram bins and bin-center precision; the expanded example fails with the older unpatched array module and passes with the upstream fixes. GAMS F1 denotes the quadratic solver, not a general iterative root finder.
