Random sampling, statistics, geometry, HDF5/FITS bindings and other modules are not selected; the example does not validate every routine in the included modules.
review_notes.fiats: Pinned Fiats tag 0.12.0 (upstream manifest version 0.11.1), named inference-engine at that revision, with an explicitly pinned compatible Julienne 1.3.1 dependency and Assert 1.7.0. Tag 0.14.0 was tried first but its consumer build cannot find Julienne modules because they are declared only as a development dependency. Single-image coarrays and long free-form lines are enabled. Based on the author's write-read-infer example, the checked consumer constructs a two-input ReLU network with known diagonal weights and biases, evaluates negative, zero and positive input pairs, and compares every output with direct formulas. K is a broad function-approximation classification; training algorithms, gradients, model-file round trips and parallel speedups are not verified. The historical version is explicit in the menu description. The original Berkeley Lab license terms, including the enhancements clause, are retained.
review_notes.julienne: Standalone demonstration of the modern Julienne testing framework, with its pinned Assert dependency and single-image coarrays. The numerical source is unchanged. The checked consumer verifies an approximate real comparison and an exact integer sum, then deliberately creates a failed test_diagnosis_t, checks its failure flag and nonempty appended diagnostic and prints it while completing successfully. This demonstrates diagnosis construction and inspection rather than macro assertion termination. The full test harness, automatic test discovery, macro enforcement and multi-image behavior are not validated. Original Berkeley Lab/Sourcery Institute license terms and dependency notices are retained.
review_notes.m-process: Unmodified Fortran/C POSIX pipe interfaces in the restricted Linux sandbox. Following the upstream process_open_read example, the consumer opens a local printf command, reads and checks the integers 7 and 11, verifies end of output and requires a successful process_close status. Commands run under the ordinary sandbox restrictions; this does not add network or host-system access. Interactive terminals, graphical subprocesses, arbitrary process behavior, write pipes and Windows portability are not verified.
review_notes.propack: Historical SciPy PROPACK 2.1 sources, whose repository is archived and explicitly points to rmlarsen/propack for the maintained implementation. The current author archive and tags v2.2/v2.1 exceed the unchanged source download limit, largely due to saved example outputs. The menu explicitly identifies this historical source choice. Only the native double-precision serial routines are wrapped, using the portable RISC modified Gram-Schmidt implementation and compatible system LP64 BLAS/LAPACK. Numerical sources are unchanged. A callback supplies multiplication by a rectangular diagonal matrix with known singular values. The consumer passes a writable convergence-count argument, requests the leading three singular triplets, and checks 12, 11 and 10, both A*v-sigma*u and transpose(A)*u-sigma*v residuals, finite values and unit vector norms. The restarted algorithm, other precisions, arbitrary sparse matrices and parallel performance are not verified.
review_notes.nufft1d: Original one-dimensional nonuniform Fourier code using the dynamically allocated Fortran 90 interface and bundled Netlib FFT implementation. Forty-nine checksum-guarded edits change legacy extent-one FFT dummy-array declarations to assumed size; every changed array is checked against its containing procedure argument list. No local arrays, transform formulas or global bounds-checking settings are changed. Legacy workspace argument type punning is accepted with the package-specific -fallow-argument-mismatch option. The example evaluates a type-1 transform of 96 deterministic nonuniform points into 32 modes for both exponent signs and compares every complex coefficient with an independent direct sum, including the documented 1/nj normalization. Status and finite values are checked. Types 2/3, the static Fortran 77 interface and every bundled FFT routine are not verified.
review_notes.nufft2d: Original two-dimensional nonuniform Fourier code using the dynamically allocated Fortran 90 interface and bundled Netlib FFT implementation. Forty-nine checksum-guarded edits change legacy extent-one FFT dummy-array declarations to assumed size after checking that each is a procedure argument; no formulas or local arrays change and bounds checking remains enabled. Legacy workspace argument type punning uses the package-specific -fallow-argument-mismatch option. The example transforms 96 deterministic scattered points onto a 16-by-18 mode grid for both exponent signs, checking status, finite values and all coefficients against an independent direct sum with the documented 1/nj normalization. Types 2/3, the static Fortran 77 interface, every FFT routine and multidimensional performance are not verified.
review_notes.aotus: Mixed C/Fortran source set selected from the upstream Waf library lists, wrapped for FPM with the bundled Lua 5.4.8 core and libraries, the C dump wrapper and GNU-supported extended/quad precision module variants. Lua command-line interpreter/compiler executables and upstream tests are excluded. Sources are unchanged; the operator-only wrapper now permits explicitly listed locked C files, retaining old adapter identities and the ordinary downloader/archive limits. The consumer creates a small Lua configuration, checks a computed integer, a double-precision scalar, two named nested-table entries and a missing-key default with error bits, closes the state and deletes its file. Broader scripting, dump/reload callbacks, every numeric kind and sandbox-restricted system operations are not verified.
review_notes.qcontainers: Explicitly selected C and Fortran library sources are wrapped for FPM. Checksum-guarded edits rename the library string conversion helper to qlibc_f_c_string and update its callers, avoiding the Fortran 2023 intrinsic name collision; container algorithms are unchanged. The unrelated qencode.c utility is excluded: its query parser refers to qstrtrim and qlisttbl routines absent from the archive. The library retains vector, list, set, hash-table and tree-table modules and their vendored C dependencies. The checked consumer exercises vector growth, indexing, replacement, array conversion, pop and clear, and string-keyed map insertion, replacement, lookup, missing-key lookup and clear. Block scope invokes finalizers. Integer payloads are used; general pointer ownership, all container methods and threading are not validated.
review_notes.stdlib-os: Mixed C/Fortran operating-system utilities wrapped for FPM. Two checksum-guarded compatibility edits set the Linux os_name constant and restrict the ISO_C_BINDING import to avoid the Fortran 2023 F_C_STRING name collision. OS_SYSTEM_ID is configured as OS_LINUX. The checked consumer creates nested temporary directories and a 14-byte stream file, checks file size and type, basename/dirname and path normalization, then renames and deletes the file and removes both directories. No external files or user environment are required. This configured recipe and exported project target Linux; Windows branches, processes, user/home lookup and every path utility are not validated.
review_notes.m_draw: Upstream mixed C/Fortran FPM library, with a checksum-guarded manifest edit adding its src/inc header directory. The X11 link dependency is retained but the checked main uses the PPM file driver, requiring no display server or Hershey font files. A 20-segment blue parabola is rendered with the PPM driver; the consumer checks P3 magic, image dimensions, color range, every pixel range and the presence of blue curve pixels. The ordinary image collector converts the generated PPM to a bounded PNG browser preview. The SVG driver aborted during font initialization when no Hershey fonts were supplied; no upstream driver code is patched, and the example uses PPM. Interactive drivers, all drawing primitives, software text/font setup and SVG output are not validated.
review_notes.fortran-lua53: Upstream Lua 5.3 bindings and source code are unchanged. A checksum-guarded manifest edit links the versioned Debian Lua 5.3 library instead of the unversioned lua name. The native development package is locked to 5.3.6-2+b4. The consumer defines a Lua function in memory, calls it for four integer arguments, independently verifies integer squares and real square roots, checks Lua status and function presence, empties the stack after each call and closes the interpreter. No files or external services are needed. Lua modules, callbacks into Fortran and arbitrary scripts are not comprehensively validated.
review_notes.netcdf-fortran: Selected serial classic-format Fortran sources follow the upstream CMake classic-library source set and use the unchanged public netCDF-C API. The operator-owned FPM wrapper retains original include files and sets HAVE_F2008, HAVE_TS29113_SUPPORT and NO_NETCDF_2 for the GNU 16 Linux environment; no library sources are edited. The native libnetcdf-dev package is locked to 1:4.9.3-1. The consumer writes a 3-by-2 real array and units attribute to a classic dataset, reopens it, checks dimension lengths, attribute and every value, then removes the file. NetCDF-4-specific Fortran interfaces, the old V2 API, parallel I/O and all data types are outside this selected build and verification scope. Source exports require the native netCDF C development library.
review_notes.scifortran: Selected integration subset, explicitly labeled in the menu: SF_INTEGRATE, GAUSS_QUADRATURE and standalone bundled QUADPACK procedures. Original include files remain in their source directories and the operator FPM wrapper compiles only the listed library files. Checksum-guarded edits promote 478 long coefficient literals from E to D exponents in DATA statements and REAL(8) PARAMETER array initializers in two bundled QUADPACK files. Each target array is checked to be REAL(8), and all decimal digits are retained. This avoids evaluating the supplied coefficients at default-real precision before assignment to double precision; formulas and the default-real compiler mode are unchanged. The linked quadrature-fortran BSD-3-Clause notice is restored as comments in GAUSS_QUADRATURE so source exports retain it. The consumer checks the Simpson and trapezoidal integrals of a sampled cubic against 1/4, adaptive integration of exp(x) over [0,1] against e-1 and exp(-x) over [0,infinity) against 1, and rejects nonfinite results. All six finite-interval Gauss-Kronrod rule choices are also checked against e-1. The example uses module callbacks: an initial consumer with internal callbacks segfaulted in the sandbox. Other SciFortran modules, MPI, linear algebra, the SCIFOR umbrella module, multidimensional/vector quadrature and all integration options are outside this selected build and verification scope.
review_notes.forpy: The existing generated upstream forpy_mod.F90 source is wrapped for FPM without running Fypp or changing the library. It embeds the sandbox Python 3.12 runtime using the linker flags advertised by python3-config --embed --ldflags, with an explicit runtime library search path. The consumer copies a 2-by-3 Fortran real64 array to NumPy, calls numpy.sum and numpy.linalg.norm, verifies both returned scalars independently in Fortran and checks finite values and every API status. Python references are destroyed before finalization. Other Python versions, no-copy array lifetimes, callbacks, Python extension modules and plotting are not validated. Exported projects need Python and NumPy and linker flags appropriate to the local Python installation.
review_notes.fkb: The upstream CMake neural library source set is wrapped for FPM in REAL64/INT32 mode with single-image coarrays and OpenMP. The deterministic consumer writes and loads a tiny two-dense-layer ReLU network, checks four predictions against independently calculated weights and biases, and verifies saving and reloading the model. K (Approximation) describes the tested neural-network inference. Training, Keras conversion tools, dropout and batch normalization are not verified; no optimization classification is inferred from their presence.
review_notes.ntpoly: The upstream Fortran library source set is wrapped for FPM with pinned MPICH and OpenBLAS native dependencies. The verified example uses exactly one MPI process, serialized MPI thread support and shared-memory/self UCX transports in the restricted sandbox. For a real symmetric positive-definite 2-by-2 matrix with eigenvalues 1 and 9, it checks SquareRoot, InverseSquareRoot and Invert against analytic matrices and independent product residuals, rejecting nonfinite values. D covers matrix functions and D2 covers inversion. Multiple MPI processes, distributed scaling, complex matrices and other solver families are outside this verification scope. Local exports require MPI/OpenBLAS development libraries and locally appropriate compiler/linker flags.
review_notes.mpifx: The upstream CMake library source list is generated with Fypp 3.2, with every generated file checksum locked in the recipe. The example exercises communicator initialization, real-vector broadcast, real and integer all-reduce and in-place maximum reduction on exactly one MPI process, checking API statuses and returned data. MPICH is pinned and UCX transports are limited to self/shared memory. This illustrates typed communication APIs, not parallel execution or speedup; point-to-point messaging, multiple processes and other wrappers are outside verification scope. Classification R covers the tested service routines.
review_notes.scalapackfx: The upstream CMake library source list is generated with Fypp 3.2 and exact generated-output checksums. The example uses a 1-by-1 BLACS grid and pinned MPICH, ScaLAPACK and OpenBLAS native libraries. It computes eigenvalues and eigenvectors of a symmetric 3-by-3 tridiagonal matrix using scalafx_psyev, checks eigenvalues against 2-sqrt(2), 2 and 2+sqrt(2), and independently checks eigenpair residuals and orthogonality. All entries must be finite. D4a1 (ordinary real symmetric eigenproblems) applies to the tested eigensolver. This is a one-process API example, not a distributed-performance demonstration; other solvers, generalized eigenproblems and multiple processes are not verified.
review_notes.easy-plplot: The existing upstream FPM package is compiled against pinned PLplot native libraries and the Cairo file driver. The main plots sine and cosine over [0,2*pi] using the pngcairo device, checks that the output file exists and is nontrivial, and the restricted sandbox must return a valid PNG preview for browser display. GUI devices, animation, interactive windows and other plotting routines are outside verification scope. Q describes the tested graphics functionality.
review_notes.gftl: gFTL is a header/template library, not a standalone compiled library. The catalog supplies a small integer-vector instantiation using the upstream v2 template, then verifies growth to 100 elements, retrieval of every stored square, and the independent sum 338350. Audited generated include files are committed as checksum-locked assets, with original m4 input hashes; generation follows the pinned CMake rules while omitting diagnostic line markers. GNU m4 on Windows and Linux reproduces identical assets. N4 covers the tested storage container. Other template/container configurations are not verified.
review_notes.gftl-shared: The catalog builds an explicitly selected subset: v1 Integer32, Integer64, default Integer, Real64, String and Unlimited vectors; StringString and Integer32Real64 maps; and v2 Integer32, Real64, String and Unlimited vectors. The consumer inserts and retrieves eight vector elements and eight map entries and verifies their sum 204. Generated v2 vector wrappers apply the upstream CMake substitutions; the original templates and Apache-2.0 notices remain intact. N4 covers container storage and N5 covers key lookup. Other upstream instantiations, sets, queues and stacks are outside this selected build and test scope. Compatible dependencies are shared through immutable exports; a source-recipe fingerprint in the FPM preprocessing profile binds generated assets and source selection to the dependency identity.
review_notes.yafyaml: The upstream YAML library is wrapped for FPM with pinned gFTL and the selected gFTL-shared containers. The checked main writes a tiny local configuration, parses an integer, a boolean, a string and an integer sequence, checks every returned value and verifies that an absent key is reported missing. Input files are removed afterwards. N1 covers configuration input and N3 covers parsing character data. The upstream parser supports a subset of YAML; full YAML conformance, all schemas and malformed-input recovery are not claimed. Source-recipe-tagged immutable dependency exports retain compatible gFTL builds.
review_notes.pflogger: The serial pFlogger library uses pinned gFTL, selected gFTL-shared containers and yaFyaml. The checked consumer writes YAML configuration, logs four severity levels to a file, and verifies that only the two expected warning/error records were accepted. MPI logging is outside this build scope. Three additional upstream v2 map instantiations are supplied as a separate checksum-locked generated asset, leaving the existing vector asset unchanged. Root COPYRIGHT identifies Apache-2.0; the historical license PDFs are retained alongside it. R covers logging service routines.
review_notes.flook: The procedural flook interface embeds the repository-bundled Lua 5.3.5 and Aotus bridge. The FPM wrapper selects the upstream procedural library and bundled C sources, excludes standalone Lua interpreters and the alternative Fortran 2003 interface, and links the system math/dynamic-loading libraries. The checked consumer passes parameters to Lua, executes a short script, retrieves its real and integer results and independently checks 14 and 21. The bundled versions have their own build context; they do not replace the separately catalogued Aotus package. MPL-2.0 and the bundled Aotus/Lua notices are retained. S covers language interoperability.
review_notes.ogpf: The checked example computes a Gaussian grid and uses the upstream contour interface to generate a PNG. A checksum-guarded catalog patch selects the headless pngcairo terminal instead of the upstream window terminal; the numerical and plotting procedures are unchanged. GNUplot is pinned as a native build dependency. The sandbox must return a browser-viewable PNG, and its preview is reviewed. MIT licensing is stated in both LICENSE and the upstream FPM manifest. Q covers graphics.
review_notes.fgsl: FGSL wraps GSL numerical routines. Broad classifications follow the exported interfaces for special functions, linear algebra, interpolation, root finding, optimization, integration/differentiation, ODEs, transforms, fitting and statistics. The checked consumer adapts the author's QAGS example and independently verifies the integral of log(x)/sqrt(x) on [0,1] against -4, status and error estimate. The procedure mapping covers adaptive one-dimensional finite-interval quadrature; other numerical interfaces are not runtime-verified by this example. Upstream Autoconf probes generated the complete configuration on GNU/Linux LP64 with GSL 2.8. An audited asset stages that header as config.inc; checksum-guarded edits change only its include filename in Fortran and C. The C support object and pinned system GSL libraries are linked. Local exports include the asset and patches; this configuration targets GNU/Linux LP64, and another ABI or GSL version requires regeneration against its local tools. GPL-2.0-or-later notices are retained.
review_notes.fdict: The current upstream Fypp templates produce fdict_types, variable and dictionary modules. Fypp 3.2 generates a checksum-locked asset with standard integer/real/complex/logical kinds, arrays through rank five, iso_fortran_env, optional extended kinds disabled and the upstream CMake default of non-pure interfaces. No CMake or Fypp runs in visitor preparation. The checked consumer stores and retrieves integer, real64, string and integer-array values, checks each returned value and frees the dictionary. N4 covers container storage and N5 covers key lookup. Earlier v0.7.1 preparation failed on missing generated includes; the current template generation resolves that blocker without downloading release assets or weakening archive checks. MPL-2.0 notices remain intact.
review_notes.flibcpp: The upstream SWIG-generated Fortran modules and C++ wrappers are built together; SWIG is not run. The upstream CMake configuration supplies only a small version-definition source. FPM 0.12 ignores .cxx, so the catalog stages unchanged wrapper contents as .cpp and preserves all original source files. The checked consumer verifies a sorted seven-element array, an existing-key position and a missing-key result. N5 and N6 classify searching and sorting, while S identifies the interoperability utility. Upstream vector, map, set, string and random facilities are included but not exercised by this consumer. MIT notices and the Apache-2.0 CMake helper notice remain intact. Local exports need compatible C++ and Fortran compilers.
review_notes.libmbd: The serial Fortran library and Fortran-written C interface are selected from the upstream CMake target and linked with pinned OpenBLAS. MPI/ScaLAPACK and ELSI are disabled. An audited version module uses an explicitly identified 0.0.0 plus pinned-commit suffix for the Git archive, rather than claiming a release version. The checked main adapts the author's argon-dimer tests at four angstrom separation, verifies dispersion energy and gradient norm against upstream reference values, checks finite results and equal/opposite gradients, and checks library exceptions. D4 covers the Hamiltonian diagonalization used by the many-body dispersion calculation; Z denotes the domain-specific physical model, not a general-purpose eigensolver interface. Other molecules, periodic systems, distributed runs and all available models are outside this consumer verification scope. MPL-2.0 notices are retained.
review_notes.dtfft: The CPU-only Fortran target is configured upstream with FFTW enabled, MPICH, input checks, and no C/C++/Python API, GPU, compression or OpenMP support. Its complete generated configuration header and source selection are checksum-locked. The checked main initializes exactly one MPI process with self/shared-memory UCX transports, transforms an 8-by-8 complex impulse, independently checks that every forward coefficient equals one, then verifies inverse reconstruction after normalization. J1 covers the multidimensional Fourier transform. Multiple processes, distributed performance and other FFT executors are not verified by this example. Local exports require compatible MPICH and FFTW development libraries and locally appropriate include/link flags. GPL-3.0-or-later notices are retained.
review_notes.dbcsr: The upstream CMake-selected serial CPU library is rendered with Fypp 3.2, with exact generated-output hashes. Simple USE lists emitted from Python sets are sorted for reproducibility across Python versions and platforms; numerical algorithms are unchanged. MPI, OpenMP, GPU, LIBXS and LIBXSMM are disabled, and the library links pinned OpenBLAS. The diagnostic filename macro uses __FILE__. The checked main creates two 4-by-4 block-sparse matrices, multiplies them through dbcsr_multiply, reconstructs the result and independently compares it with MATMUL, requiring finite entries and a small maximum error. D1 covers matrix operations. Parallel scaling, accelerators and tensor operations are outside this verification scope. GPL-2.0-or-later notices are retained. The wrapper repeats the base-hooks USE list so FPM can order dependencies hidden in the original include. Its manifest permits legacy implicit external BLAS/LAPACK calls; runtime and bounds checks remain enabled.
review_notes.2decomp-fft: The upstream CMake-selected CPU library uses the built-in generic Fourier transform backend, double precision and pinned MPICH. OpenMP is disabled. The example adapts the author-provided complex FFT example, initializes exactly one MPI process with self/shared-memory UCX transports, transforms an 8-by-6-by-4 complex impulse, independently checks that all forward coefficients equal one, and verifies inverse reconstruction after normalization. J1 covers the multidimensional Fourier transform. Multiple MPI processes and distributed performance are not verified. Local exports need compatible MPI development libraries and locally appropriate include/link flags. BSD-3-Clause notices are retained.
review_notes.ennuf: The pinned upstream neural_net_mod module is compiled with an audited, generated fixed-weight model: two inputs, two ReLU hidden units and one output in REAL32. Operator generation uses the author Model/Dense/Activation API and NumPy 2.2.6; neither TensorFlow, PyTorch nor Python inference runs in visitor jobs. The generator sorts the imported layer routine names for reproducibility; network operations are unchanged. Four inputs exercise positive and clipped hidden units and predictions are checked against independently evaluated weights and biases, including negative and positive outputs and finiteness. K covers inference as approximation; no least-squares fitting or training classification is inferred. The sample network is illustrative, not a trained scientific model. Other network layers, external model conversion and training are not verified. BSD-3-Clause and Crown copyright notices are retained.
review_notes.ddpcm: The pinned ddCOSMO library and original fixed-form Lebedev quadrature source are wrapped for FPM with extension-based source form and legacy external interfaces. OpenMP directives are inactive in this serial profile and OpenBLAS supplies dense linear algebra. The checked consumer adapts the author main and formaldehyde input, embedding its four-atom coordinates, radii, charges and solver settings. It compares solvation energy and all force components against the author reference output, requires finite values and checks zero net force. Full-sized dummy arrays replace the unused one-element placeholders in the example while leaving library numerical routines unchanged. D2 identifies the Jacobi/DIIS linear-system solution used by cosmo; Z denotes the physical solvation model. Other molecules, solvent parameters, quantum densities and parallel performance are outside this verification scope. LGPL notices and author reference requests remain in the source tree.
review_notes.dftd4: The original FPM library and pinned mctc-lib, multicharge, Jonquil and TOML-F dependencies are compiled with GNU Fortran 16.2.0 and pinned OpenBLAS. Jonquil and mctc-lib request different TOML-F tags; the operator recipe resolves both to the mctc-lib-requested 0.4.2 commit, checksummed in the dependency lock. The checked consumer adapts the upstream test_pbed4_mb01 reference and embeds MB16-43/01 geometry from mstore v0.4.0, retaining its Apache-2.0 attribution. PBE-D4 two-body energy is compared with -0.018578752883363366 Hartree to 1e-10 Hartree. It also checks finite results, zero net force, translation invariance and one analytical gradient component against a central finite difference with step 1e-5 bohr and tolerance 1e-6. Z denotes the physical dispersion model; no general-purpose differentiation or linear-system interface is inferred from its internal calculations. Other molecules, periodic systems, D4S, three-body terms and all gradients are outside this consumer verification scope. No numerical library source edits are applied; all dependencies use immutable shared archive exports. LGPL-3.0-or-later and dependency notices are retained.
review_notes.ftorch: The original FTorch Fortran and C++ sources are wrapped for FPM, using pinned Debian CPU LibTorch 2.6.0+dfsg-7, the C++20 mode, C++11 ABI and include/definition settings from the upstream CMake target. The operator C++ flag setting is restricted to a current, unshared source-package recipe; public requests cannot set it and previous cache keys are preserved. The self-contained consumer embeds a reproducibly generated 1,766-byte TorchScript model as hexadecimal text, writes tiny.pt in the sandbox and calls the author tensor/model API in REAL64. Two different five-element inputs exercise y=2*x+1, with each output checked independently for finiteness and absolute error below 1e-12. The second call also verifies that the input tensor observes updated Fortran storage. No Python or model download runs in visitor jobs. This is an illustrative affine inference model, not a trained scientific predictor. K covers inference as function approximation; no training or optimization classification is inferred. GPU use, training, autograd, parallel execution and arbitrary external models are not verified. FTorch MIT notices and native Debian dependency notices are retained. APT estimates about 924 MB of additional native dependencies in the isolated FTorch image; these are separate from the catalog logical library-artifact total.
review_notes.tsunami: Only the author serial Chapter 4 mod_diff and mod_initial modules are wrapped; their contents are unchanged. The main follows the chapter shallow-water time-stepping equations on a 100-cell periodic grid for 200 steps. It checks the centered difference against a discrete sine derivative, the upwind difference against an independently indexed periodic reference, Gaussian peak/symmetry, finite water height/velocity, positive total depth, nontrivial evolution, and conservation of integrated elevation. The example uses REAL32, with REAL64 accumulation of mass. I2 classifies the demonstrated PDE calculation; H1 classifies diff_centered/diff_upwind as numerical differentiation. This is an educational finite-difference demonstration, not validation of a production tsunami model. Other chapters, coarrays and parallel scaling are not verified. MIT notices are retained.
review_notes.pfunit: The pinned serial pFUnit configuration disables MPI, OpenMP, robust/forked runners and Hamcrest, and uses the author-supported MAX_ASSERT_RANK=2 option (scalars, vectors and matrices) to retain the existing 2 MiB generated-source asset limit. The author CMake configuration supplies source selections and compiler-kind definitions; overload_template.py generates the assertions. fArgParse and its gFTL-shared/gFTL submodules are pinned at the exact upstream gitlinks, with only the required shared container instantiations generated. The FPM scanner sees a NAG-only f90_unix_proc USE even on GNU, so that inactive branch is declared external; inactive robust/Hamcrest interfaces are likewise excluded without altering original library code. A plain Fortran main constructs three TestMethod cases in a TestSuite and checks scalar, vector and matrix assertions through TestRunner/SerialContext, requiring exactly three runs and zero errors/failures. No visitor-side Python, CMake or annotation generation is needed. Higher assertion ranks, matcher DSLs, MPI, OpenMP and process-forking runners are not offered by this configuration. S denotes software testing; no numerical solver classification is inferred. Apache-2.0 and dependency notices are retained.
review_notes.raffle: RAFFLE is pinned to release v1.0.0 because current main and v1.1.1 exceed the unchanged 16 MiB archive limit. The native FPM library is unchanged. The checked main adapts test/test_dist_calcs.f90: a two-atom silicon primitive cell and three equivalent fractional points exercise get_min_dist_between_point_and_atom and get_min_dist. Both distances must be finite and agree with sqrt(3)*0.428 within 3e-6 in REAL32. P denotes the demonstrated periodic geometry; no optimization, structure-prediction accuracy, trained model, or full upstream test-suite validation is claimed. GPL-3.0 notices are retained.
review_notes.plplot: The unmodified PLplot 5.15.0 modern Fortran binding modules are compiled with GNU Fortran 16 against Debian libplplot 5.15.0+dfsg2-15+b1. The author CMake precision template is configured with c_double to match the native double-precision C core; the generated include is checksum-locked. Original included parameter/interface sources and LGPL notices are retained. The checked main follows the author plinit/plenv/pllab/plline/plend API, checks finite sine samples and known extrema, requests the headless pngcairo driver at 800x500, and verifies the generated PNG signature and nontrivial size. The sandbox must return a browser-viewable PNG, which is visually reviewed. Q covers graphics. Native C/Cairo libraries and fonts are installed only in this package image; no precompiled Debian Fortran module files are used by the consumer. Interactive windows, other output drivers and the full upstream example/test suite are not verified.
review_notes.fortran-curl: Release 0.8.0 is pinned because its documented libcurl minimum is 8.10.0, compatible with the pinned Debian libcurl 8.14.1-2+deb13u7; current main requires 8.20.0. The original FPM library and C helpers are unchanged. The example adapts examples/url/url.f90 and checks successful URL parsing plus exact host, path, port and query strings, changes the path and checks the reconstructed URL. The C URL handle is released and cleared by the caller, following the 0.8 cleanup semantics. N3 describes parsing/constructing character data. No network request is made; sandbox internet access remains disabled. HTTP transfers, authentication, mail protocols and other libcurl facilities are not runtime-verified. ISC notices are retained.
review_notes.m_history: The unmodified M_history redo editor records two commands in its scratch history file. The self-contained main supplies editing directives through the optional lun argument, recalls line 1, changes 290 to 300 and checks the result, then recalls line 2 and verifies that its original text remains unchanged. No shell command is executed and no interactive terminal is required. The main follows the author application in using a 1024-character buffer. An initial 120-character buffer triggered an upstream bounds error at cin(1:255); that diagnostic is retained separately, and shorter buffers are not verified/supported by this catalog example. N1/N3 cover command input and character editing; no numerical-method classification is inferred. MIT library notices and the public-domain author application notice are retained.
review_notes.m_cli: The original M_CLI FPM library is unchanged. The checked consumer adapts the author example/demo3.f90, translating a prototype command into NAMELIST text and checking integer, real, logical, character and three-element real array defaults before using the scaled sum. No stdin or program arguments are required; the editable prototype supplies the defaults. Actual command-line overrides, help/error paths and interactive examples are not runtime-verified here. N1/N3 cover command input and character parsing; no numerical-method classification is inferred. Public-domain/Unlicense notices are retained.
review_notes.fortran-modbus: The original Fortran 2018 FPM bindings are compiled against pinned Debian libmodbus 3.1.11-2. The consumer checks positive, negative and zero single-precision values through the ABCD, BADC, CDAB and DCBA register conversion APIs and prints register words in hexadecimal. These are offline operations, with no socket, serial port or Modbus device. N2 covers bit/byte representation; the catalog does not claim verified device communication. The author test/test_modbus.f90 documents context use but is not used as a device test. ISC notices are retained.
review_notes.gtk-fortran: The original gtk-fortran 4.8.0 FPM manifest is unchanged and builds the core bindings and high-level helper modules. GNU 16 compilation initially stopped in gtk-hl-dialog.f90 because f_c_string was resolved as a function rather than the legacy subroutine alias. Eleven checksum-guarded call-name replacements use the equivalent convert_f_string generic already provided by gtk_sup, matching current upstream spelling; arguments and implementations are unchanged. The unpatched diagnostic is retained. This release targets GTK 4.18.4/GLib 2.84.1 and is linked against pinned Debian GTK 4.18.6, with Cairo 1.18.4. The example adapts the author Cairo drawing API to an image surface, checks Cairo statuses and PNG signature/size, and draws curves, circles and text without gtk_init, a window or a display server. The returned browser preview is visually reviewed. Q covers graphics. Desktop widgets, events, interactive GUI sessions and the full upstream tests are not runtime-verified. GPL-3.0-or-later with GCC Runtime Library Exception 3.1 notices are retained.
review_notes.fycollections: The original FyCollections backend and author examples/list/type_intlist.fpp and type_stringlist.fpp are generated with Fypp 3.2 without changing their algorithms. Six generated Fortran files, checksums of all template/license inputs, and xgenerate_fycollections.py retain a reproducible recipe. The package supplies the author IntList and StringList specializations, not automatic runtime generation for arbitrary user types. Its operator FPM wrapper uses version 0.0.0 to identify no inferred upstream release; the source is pinned by commit. The checked main adapts the author integer/string list examples and checks append, insertion, retrieval, successful/missing searches, integer deletion and allocatable-list finalization. N4/N5 cover storage containers and searching. Pointer/array list specializations and the complete upstream tests are not verified. BSD-2-Clause notices are retained.
review_notes.fortran-sdl2: The original FPM library and Fortran bindings are unchanged. The image pins SDL 2.32.4, SDL2_image 2.8.8, SDL2_mixer 2.8.1, SDL2_ttf 2.24.0 and GL/GLU development libraries; native link flags are recorded in the catalog build environment. The checked main creates a 640x360 32-bit software surface, fills a background and three bars, checks source pixels, saves a PNG, reloads it through the package IMG_Load API, and checks dimensions plus the file signature/size. The pinned bindings omit IMG_SavePNG, so the main includes only that standard C function declaration. No image encoder or drawing algorithm is substituted for SDL. No video subsystem, window, display server, hardware renderer, audio device or event loop is needed. The returned browser preview is visually reviewed. Q covers graphics. Interactive rendering, audio, fonts and OpenGL/GLU routines are compiled/linked facilities but not runtime-verified by this consumer. ISC notices are retained.
